name: Azarun
stage: Playable AI Trailer Reel & Custom LoRA
media_label: ACTUAL PRODUCTION FRAME · KLING AI + RUNPOD LORA
image_caption: Production environment keyframe from the Azarun trailer pipeline (Kling AI, Seedance & custom Runpod LoRA azarun_god_v1).
tagline: A cinematic AI trailer introducing an African mythological hero—engineered with custom Runpod GPU LoRA training (azarun_god_v1) for cross-shot character consistency.
overview: Azarun is the debut installment in a generative visual storytelling series showcasing African mythological heroes. Developed across Kling AI, Seedance, Gemini, and ChatGPT—and anchored by custom character-consistency models trained on Runpod GPU infrastructure—the project demonstrates disciplined visual continuity across multi-shot AI cinema.
problem: Generative video pipelines frequently break immersion across edits as character anatomy, facial features, and wardrobe drift from shot to shot. Sustaining cinematic credibility requires controlled dataset curation, custom model training, and iterative shot evaluation.
concept: Treat AI video production with traditional film-direction discipline: lock hero identity through custom GPU LoRA weights first, establish cohesive basalt-and-ember worldbuilding keyframes, and then direct controlled motion sequences shot by shot.
role: AI & Content Specialist, Model Trainer (Runpod), Prompt Direction & Creative Production
approach: Curated consistent character reference sets, trained multi-checkpoint LoRA weights (azarun_god_v1) on Runpod GPU infrastructure, evaluated outputs across checkpoints to eliminate drift, and orchestrated motion generation across Kling AI and Seedance.
features: Custom character-consistency LoRA training (azarun_god_v1) and checkpoint evaluation on Runpod GPUs
Shot-by-shot prompt architecture and camera choreography across Kling AI, Seedance, Gemini, and GPT
Locked hero identity (facial geometry, braids, glowing eyes, pauldrons, obsidian armor, and battle-axe) across independent scenes
Four web-playable rendered trailer sequences spanning slow reveals, audio-synced motion, volcanic environments, and end-screen finishing
decisions: Rather than relying on zero-shot prompting alone, investing upfront in custom Runpod LoRA training reduced re-roll waste and preserved recognizable protagonist continuity across dramatic lighting shifts.
outcome: Produced a multi-shot trailer reel and verified character-consistency checkpoint suite; four native MP4 clips and side-by-side LoRA renders are embedded directly on this page.

name: Irysnameservice
image_caption: Irys Names dApp interface featuring .irys domain search, EVM & Solana wallet integration, Test SOL faucet, and Rewards.
tagline: Founded an on-chain .irys domain-minting, mutable-reference transfer, and Proof-of-Vibe onboarding dApp—documented in CV as reaching #1 dApp in the Irys ecosystem.
overview: Irysnameservice (Irys Names) allows users to search, mint, and permanently store .irys domain identities on the Irys datachain across EVM and Solana wallets. Beyond minting, it includes a 5-step mutable-reference domain transfer workflow, permanent on-chain Certificates of Ownership, and interactive GraphQL flashcards.
problem: Emerging blockchain datachains need approachable consumer identity products—paired with clear developer education and community distribution—to turn ecosystem interest into sustained on-chain interaction.
concept: Combine permanent on-chain naming with frictionless multi-chain onboarding (EVM + Solana + built-in Test SOL faucet), verifiable ownership certificates, and bite-sized ecosystem learning cards.
approach: Defined the core minting, transfer, and certificate flows around Irys's permanent storage and mutable-reference primitives, while pairing product launches with community outreach and Solana Ambassador demonstration.
features: Permanent .irys domain search and minting stored directly on the Irys datachain
Multi-chain wallet connection (EVM & Solana) with built-in Test SOL faucet, Rewards, and Pricing views
5-step Domain Ownership Transfer workflow (Verify → Configure → Confirm → Processing → Complete) built on Irys mutable references
On-chain Certificates of Ownership recording domain tier, mint cost, timestamp, and transaction hash
Interactive IRYS Flashcards (Proof of Vibe) teaching GraphQL indexing and datachain fundamentals
decisions: Pairing functional domain transfers with shareable Ownership Certificates and interactive flashcards turned one-off testnet mints into repeat community education and organic sharing.
outcome: Documented in CV as becoming the #1 dApp in the Irys ecosystem; a 1-minute walkthrough video and four real product captures are preserved directly in this case study.

name: Project Mucci
image_caption: Live authentication entry portal at project-mucci.web.app (Google OAuth & invitation-gated cohort onboarding).
tagline: A cohort mentorship command center for running structured programs, reviewing daily check-ins, and delivering image-annotated feedback with Firebase RBAC.
overview: Project Mucci gives mentors and cohorts a dedicated workspace for daily accountability. Mentors create programs, invite cohorts securely, track daily mentee check-ins, and return annotated visual feedback—backed by Firebase authentication, Firestore membership rules, and automated authorization tests.
problem: Mentorship cohorts frequently scatter across messaging apps and shared spreadsheets, making it difficult to enforce program membership boundaries, track consistent daily progress, or preserve structured feedback over time.
concept: Build an invitation-gated mentor-and-mentee command center where daily progress logs, visual critique, and strict Firestore access controls live in a single reliable workspace.
role: Product Direction, Full-Stack Implementation & Authorization Testing
approach: Engineered the frontend in React, TypeScript, and Vite backed by Firebase Auth, Firestore, and Storage rules, with Vitest authorization tests validating program access and member removal.
features: Cohort program setup with Google OAuth and email-invitation onboarding
Daily mentee progress check-ins with status tracking and mentor review queues
Mentor feedback supporting direct image annotations for visual correction
Firebase authentication, Firestore-backed membership schema, and Storage security rules
Vitest security and authorization tests covering program access and member removal
decisions: Assignments, grading, and analytics modules were intentionally kept locked in the current build so core check-in workflows and Firestore authorization boundaries could be hardened first.
outcome: Deployed live on Firebase Hosting (project-mucci.web.app) with public source and authorization tests documented in GitHub.

name: MedFlash (MCQ Recall)
image_caption: Live dark-mode board review workspace at mcqrecall.netlify.app.
tagline: A physician-built board review application that converts raw multiple-choice question PDFs into structured active-recall study sessions.
overview: Born directly from medical exam preparation, MedFlash (MCQ Recall) turns uploaded multi-file MCQ PDFs into focused active-recall study sessions—paired with a built-in Pomodoro timer, session history, and a low-fatigue dark interface.
problem: Medical students and doctors preparing for board exams routinely waste hours reformatting past-question PDFs instead of practicing active recall under timed conditions.
concept: Remove setup friction completely: drop one or more MCQ PDFs into the browser, treat each document as a resumable study session, and pair active recall with an integrated Pomodoro workflow.
role: Clinical Creator, Product Design & Web Implementation
approach: Built a zero-signup client-side web workflow deployed to Netlify, featuring multi-file PDF drag-and-drop ingestion (supporting 'Correct Answer X' formatting) and four focused navigation views: Sessions, Pomodoro, History, and Settings.
features: Multi-file drag-and-drop PDF uploader with automatic MCQ and answer-key parsing
Session-based workspace turning every uploaded PDF into a resumable study deck
Built-in Pomodoro focus timer for high-volume medical revision blocks
Persistent study history and customizable review settings in a distraction-free dark UI
decisions: Eliminating account walls and supporting multi-file PDF drops directly on the landing screen ensured students can move from raw past questions to active recall in seconds.
outcome: Live and publicly accessible at mcqrecall.netlify.app.

name: Kasala
image_caption: Live lobby capture from kasala.kasala.workers.dev displaying four playable 3D Lagos character classes and match modes.
tagline: A ten-player browser battle royale and 5v5 arena shooter set in Computer Village, Lagos—built with an AI-assisted 3D asset pipeline and deployed on Cloudflare Workers.
overview: Kasala brings compact multiplayer 3D action directly to the browser without app-store downloads. Set in Computer Village, Lagos, it supports Solo and Team Battle Royale, 5v5 Team Battle, Free-for-All, configurable AI bots, and a Gun Range.
problem: 3D multiplayer shooters are traditionally locked behind heavy native installs and large studio pipelines, leaving culturally grounded West African settings rarely represented in instant web games.
concept: Pair an AI-assisted 3D character and audio production workflow with lightweight browser delivery on Cloudflare Workers so players can launch matches in one click.
role: Game Direction, AI-Assisted 3D Asset & Audio Pipeline, Cloudflare Deployment
approach: Directed character creation across four recognizable Lagos archetypes, structured multiple match modes (Battle Royale, 5v5, Free-for-All, Bots, Gun Range), and shipped globally on Cloudflare Workers.
features: Ten-player online Battle Royale (Solo & Teams) plus 5v5 Team Battle and Free-for-All
Online matchmaking, private friend lobbies, Bot difficulty levels (Easy / Medium / Hard), and Gun Range
Four custom AI-assisted 3D character renders and full audio/music direction
Zero-install browser play delivered via Cloudflare Workers
decisions: Including offline-friendly bot tiers and a dedicated Gun Range alongside online lobbies ensures solo visitors can experience gameplay immediately even outside peak lobby hours.

name: Wayo: Naija Hide & Seek
image_caption: Live lobby capture from playwayo.netlify.app — Raid in Progress.
tagline: A phone-first 3D multiplayer prop hunt set in Computer Village, Ikeja—traders disguise as market goods while the Task Force searches before time runs out.
overview: Wayo transforms an iconic Lagos street-market dynamic into an accessible 3D multiplayer game. Traders disguise themselves as everyday marketplace objects while the Task Force conducts a four-minute raid.
problem: Social prop-hunt games are typically desktop-bound and detached from local Nigerian humor and mobile-first play patterns.
concept: Design a landscape-first 3D browser prop hunt with instant five-letter room codes, host-controlled match starts, and solo bot practice.
approach: Built as a lightweight HTML/JavaScript 3D web application with online room lobbies, configurable look-speed controls, custom soundtrack toggles, and Netlify deployment.
features: 3D prop-hunt gameplay modeled on Computer Village, Ikeja
Online multiplayer rooms with five-letter join codes and shareable invitations
Solo bot practice mode alongside timed four-minute multiplayer raids
Mobile landscape-first ergonomics with full desktop support and sensitivity settings
decisions: Keeping room joining to a five-letter code and adding a 'Practise with bots' link directly under the lobby actions minimized friction for mobile players.
outcome: Live and playable at playwayo.netlify.app with source available on GitHub.

name: Naija Undead
image_caption: Live 3D WebGL scene from naijaundead.fun — City 1: Ojuelegba, Lagos.
tagline: A mobile-first 3D Lagos zombie survival game directed and launched end-to-end with an AI-assisted character and audio production workflow.
overview: Set in City 1: Ojuelegba, Lagos, Naija Undead challenges players to survive twelve-minute nights with a cutlass against localized undead archetypes—Traffic Hawker, Mama Put, Conductor, Agbero, Mechanic, and Politician—while completing nightly bounty jobs.
problem: Producing stylized 3D character rosters, atmospheric audio, and mobile browser combat normally demands multi-person studio budgets.
concept: Use AI-assisted 3D character and sound workflows to rapidly direct and launch a culturally unmistakable Lagos survival game directly to the web.
role: Game Director, AI Asset & Audio Pipeline, Web Launch
approach: Combined mobile-vertical 3D WebGL framing, localized enemy design, Naira bounty progression, and personal-best tracking into an immediately playable browser deployment.
features: Real-time 3D WebGL survival action in a stylized Ojuelegba, Lagos nightscape
Localized undead roster (Traffic Hawker, Mama Put, Conductor, Agbero, Mechanic & Politician)
Twelve-minute night runs with nightly job bounties and persistent personal-best tracking
Mobile-first vertical viewport with audio and display toggles
decisions: Embracing a centered vertical mobile-proportioned viewport kept frame pacing clean on phones while looking intentionally composed on desktop.

name: Hodos
media_label: CONCEPTUAL EDITORIAL PLATE · SOURCE ON GITHUB
image_caption: Editorial visual plate representing Hodos's guided AI career-pathway architecture (codebase inspected on GitHub).
tagline: An AI career-direction web application combining conversational assessment, personalized pathways, skill-gap diagnostics, and serverless Anthropic & Airtable functions.
overview: Hodos is built for people entering the AI economy who want clarity on where their existing strengths fit. A guided conversational assessment routes through serverless Netlify Functions calling the Anthropic API to generate tailored career pathways, skill-gap breakdowns, and starter projects, persisted in Airtable.
problem: Generic career advice ignores individual backgrounds, actionable skill gaps, and locally relevant opportunities in fast-moving AI markets.
concept: Guide users through a lightweight multi-step web assessment (index, assessment, results) backed by structured Claude prompts and Airtable persistence.
approach: Implemented the frontend flow in HTML, CSS, and JavaScript connected to serverless Netlify Functions integrating the Anthropic API and Airtable.
features: Conversational strengths and career-direction assessment workflow
Serverless Netlify Functions orchestrating Anthropic Claude API calls
AI-generated personalized direction summaries, skill-gap diagnostics, and starter project ideas
Airtable integration for structured assessment persistence
decisions: Keeping the frontend dependency-free while isolating Anthropic API keys inside Netlify Functions created a fast, auditable serverless architecture.
outcome: Functional codebase published publicly on GitHub (hermes-nietzesch/hodos-site); public deployment pending.

name: MedForge AI
image_caption: Editorial visualization representing MedForge AI's clinical study workspace prototype (React/TypeScript codebase on GitHub).
tagline: A multi-screen React clinical learning prototype uniting generated study timetables, note ingestion flows, OSCE practice, MCQ views, and an AI mentor interface.
overview: MedForge AI explores how clinical medical education can become more structured and personalized. The repository implements a multi-screen React, TypeScript, and Tailwind interface covering study planning, learning confidence analysis, OSCE drills, and mentor conversation views.
problem: Medical students juggle dense lecture notes, ward rotations, MCQs, and practical OSCE stations across disconnected tools that rarely reflect clinical reasoning workflows.
concept: Design a unified clinical learning studio modeled on real MBBS preparation—bringing timetables, note review, confidence heatmaps, and AI mentor guidance under one roof.
approach: Built modular React + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS views with Vite to validate information architecture and multi-screen study journeys using illustrative clinical data.
features: Study dashboard and generated clinical timetable views
Handwritten-note and document-upload workflow concepts
High-yield notes, MCQ review, and OSCE preparation interfaces
AI mentor conversation view alongside confidence heatmaps and weekly learning insights
decisions: Prototyping the complete multi-screen study UX first with structured illustrative datasets allows rapid iteration with medical students before wiring live clinical LLM backends.
outcome: Public React/TypeScript interface prototype available on GitHub (live AI backend not yet connected).

name: VitalPulse
image_caption: Editorial visualization representing VitalPulse's emergency blood-donor response concept (private repository prototype).
tagline: A healthcare emergency-response prototype exploring blood-donor alerts, urgency prioritization, donor education, and rapid alert acceptance flows.
overview: VitalPulse explores how mobile-first digital design can make urgent blood-donation needs clearer and more actionable. Built in a private React/TypeScript repository, the prototype models the full donor journey from urgent request alert to acceptance confirmation and impact reporting using illustrative emergency data.
problem: Emergency blood requests frequently circulate as unstructured social messages lacking clarity on urgency, blood type, or next steps—creating friction when minutes matter.
concept: Replace chaotic appeals with a calm, high-clarity mobile donor interface featuring structured urgency cards, guided confirmation flows, and donor education.
approach: Engineered mobile-friendly interactive flows in React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and Vite demonstrating emergency donor alerts, profiles, educational sections, and confirmation states.
features: Emergency blood-donor request screens with clear urgency details
Alert acceptance and confirmation demonstration workflow
Donor profile, clinical eligibility learning, and personal impact views
Mobile-first navigation and restrained interface motion
decisions: Focusing the prototype on donor clarity and low-stress confirmation steps directly reflects clinical observations of blood-sourcing friction; uses illustrative example requests rather than live hospital matching.
outcome: Interactive prototype maintained in a private repository; available for walkthrough upon request.
